parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/mailer/mailer.service.ts is placed in the application layer because of its *.service.ts suffix, but it contains no use-case or orchestration logic. It works only as a technical adapter. It builds and owns an SMTP transport with nodemailer, configured from the connection settings (host, port, TLS and auth credentials). It reads template files from disk with node:fs/promises, compiles them with Handlebars, and sends mail over SMTP. Talking to an external transport, reading the file system and rendering templates are infrastructure work. The application-level orchestration lives in MailService (src/mail/mail.service.ts), which injects this class as a dependency. So this file takes on infrastructure work while declared as application.

violations.message: MailerService is declared as application layer but does infrastructure work. These belong in an infrastructure adapter, for example src/infrastructure/mailer, behind a port that the application layer uses.
